clue.text: Astonishment about one king after another making suicidal attack

indicators.note: the first king and its surroundings come after another king, so that king goes in front

parts.note: another king, K being the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the astonishment word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: astonishment is what you feel when things amaze you; here the verb AMAZE
one is the Roman numeral I
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A war report: amazement as one king follows another in a reckless suicidal assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and K inside AMAZE to give AMIKAZE; 'after another' puts a second K in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese wartime pilots flew planes deliberately into targets, so the word names any suicidal attack.

clue.text: This hour featured in The Charge of the Light Brigade?

definitions.text: This hour featured in The Charge of the Light Brigade?

parts.words: This hour featured in The Charge of the Light Brigade?
parts.note: read charge as an electricity bill for lighting: the unit billed is a thousand watts used for an hour

explanation.surface: Asking what hour appears in Tennyson's poem of the cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity is charged by the unit of a thousand watts sustained for one hour, so lighting bills feature it.

clue.text: Oxbridge college East may leave for another

definitions.text: Oxbridge college East may leave for another

parts.words: Oxbridge college East may leave for another
parts.note: the Cambridge college's name ends in E, for East; drop it and the spelling is that of the Oxford college

explanation.surface: A university college from which East might decamp to a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxbridge means Oxford and Cambridge together; the two universities have colleges whose names differ only by a final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cambridge college bears this name, and the Oxford college spells the same saint's name without the final letter.

clue.text: Hill Minor makes bad joke about Prince

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled joke wraps round the next piece
bad signals that the letters of joke are spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy called Minor tells a poor joke about a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' reworks JOKE into KOJE; 'about' puts P inside it. A kopje is a small hill on the South African veld.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans for a small rocky outcrop, so it means a little hill.

clue.text: Very keen, the Greek god, to get a look in

indicators.note: in at the end places the preceding pieces inside the god's name

parts.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Eager, the chief of Olympus wants to have a peek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' only joins; LO is the old exclamation 'lo and behold', meaning look.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing great fervour or eagerness, this word means extremely enthusiastic.

clue.text: Just a shake, in Robin Hood's case

definitions.meaning: the container in which the legendary archer carried his arrows

explanation.surface: A tremble in the outlaw's arrow holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight tremble is a shiver of that name, and an archer like the outlaw keeps arrows in a case of that name.

clue.text: Railwaymen unusually happy? History is silent

indicators.note: unusually says the union's letters come in an unusual order

parts.note: NUR is the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union
elated means very happy

explanation.surface: Union rail workers are oddly cheerful, but the records say nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges NUR to UNR. Related means told or narrated, so something unrelated is a matter on which history says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to narrate, so a thing nobody has recounted is one the chronicles stay quiet about.

clue.text: Bosom traitor

parts.note: a betrayer one has cherished, from the saying about nursing a snake in one's breast

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a snake in one's bosom' names a treacherous person who was trusted, this venomous adder being the snake.

clue.text: Madness so near to sanity

indicators.note: madness suggests disorder, so the letters of so near go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Insanity lies close to soundness of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's wits is losing one's mind, the same as losing a rational faculty.

clue.text: Anticipate this all for 18's starter

parts.note: the first part of the answer to 18 down is the name of a Shakespearean woodland; put this word in front of it to name the wood

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to get ahead of the first part of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 down begins ARDEN, the setting of As You Like It; 'Anticipate' means go before, so this word precedes it as the Forest of Arden.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy is set in a woodland of that name, so this word precedes the name in full.

clue.text: High kick helps one into the saddle for instance

definitions.meaning: a leg raised high, read literally

definitions.text: helps one into the saddle for instance
definitions.meaning: a boost given to a rider mounting, or any helpful start

explanation.surface: A dancer's high kick doubles as the boost given to a rider mounting a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a leg is a high kick, and a boost of that name lifts a rider into the saddle, or helps anyone get started.

clue.text: Bible stories never told by the canon

definitions.text: Bible stories never told by the canon

parts.words: Bible stories never told by the canon
parts.note: a cathedral canon is a clergyman, but the canon is also the accepted list of scripture; these books were left out of it

explanation.surface: Biblical tales a cathedral clergyman never preaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The disputed books excluded from the accepted biblical canon form a group of writings considered not authentic scripture.

clue.text: Henry, trapped by Spider, has one stiffener

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside, so the next piece sits within the spider's work

parts.note: a spider's work is its WEB
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Henry is caught by a spider, and somehow gains something stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V; 'has' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plates from a whale's mouth were used to stiffen corsets and collars.

clue.text: Handle, say, a regular go-slow? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words regular go-slow is used, a run within them

explanation.surface: A trade-union wrangle about handling regular go-slow tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle, say' is Handel, spelt as it sounds: his most famous slow aria is known as his Largo.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Handel's best-known slow piece is called by this tempo marking, so the name stands for a work of his.

clue.text: With 50 litres, squiffy crisscross effect

indicators.note: squiffy means slightly drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: After fifty litres of drink, someone's vision goes tipsy and criss-crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of crossed wooden strips for climbing plants makes a crisscross pattern.

clue.text: Eleventh-hour recovery is made sideways

parts.note: something at the eleventh hour comes late
a rally is a recovery, as in a market or a patient

explanation.surface: A last-minute comeback is made by moving sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to the side rather than forwards is travelling on a horizontal course.

clue.text: Make lace edging also to decorate the body

parts.note: to tat is to make knotted lace, such as edging, by hand
too means also

explanation.surface: Making a lace border, and decorating one's skin too.
explanation.definitionFit: Inking designs into the skin is how one adorns the body permanently.

clue.text: One over bust could be so unwelcome

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be arranged into a different word

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A large bust might be too prominent and so unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges I, OVER and BUST; 'so' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrusive sticks out where it is not wanted, so it is unwanted.

clue.text: How a lover sighed first, where was Jaques?

definitions.text: How a lover sighed first, where was Jaques?

parts.words: How a lover sighed first, where was Jaques?
parts.note: a lover sighs passionately; and the first part of the word is the forest where Jaques, the melancholy lord in As You Like It, lived

explanation.surface: A question about a sighing lover and where a Shakespeare character spent his exile.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer begins ARDEN, the forest of As You Like It, where Jaques gives his speech on the seven ages of man, including the sighing lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaques describes 'the lover, sighing like furnace', so the lover sighs passionately.

clue.text: Pill-pounder made from soft steel

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

indicators.note: made from says the next word is the raw material, reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's grinding tool forged from mild steel.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, p (piano) instructs the player to play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A club-shaped tool grinds pills and other substances to powder in a mortar.

clue.text: He checks account of a Rhodesian breakaway to the right

parts.note: UDI, the Unilateral Declaration of Independence by which Rhodesia broke from Britain in 1965
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone reports on Rhodesia's split from Britain and the drift to the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who examines a firm's books inspects its finances for accuracy.

clue.text: Endearing feature of man met on the stair?

definitions.text: Endearing feature of man met on the stair?

parts.words: Endearing feature of man met on the stair?
parts.note: it is said to make the heart grow fonder, and the man met on the stair in the rhyme 'wasn't there'

explanation.surface: Asking what is lovable about a stranger encountered on the staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: Two sayings: 'Absence makes the heart grow fonder', and Hughes Mearns's rhyme 'Yesterday upon the stair, I met a man who wasn't there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away is proverbially what makes hearts fonder, and the man on the stair was simply not present.

clue.text: Joseph takes on the gunners in the Diplomatic Corps

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: CD stands for Corps Diplomatique, the diplomatic corps
taken as written
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A man named Joseph takes on the army's artillery while serving among diplomats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish-born English novelist of Heart of Darkness had this first name.

clue.text: Ring around a magpie

parts.note: on a shooting target the magpie is a ring near the edge, and the band beyond it encircles it

explanation.surface: A circle forming round a black-and-white bird.
explanation.definitionFit: On a rifle target the band outside the magpie is the outermost scoring ring.

clue.text: The theme to choose is incomplete

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: incomplete says the word is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: The subject to be selected has not been fully decided.
explanation.definitionFit: The subject of a talk or essay is what it is about.

clue.text: Step on it the proverbial decelerator

definitions.meaning: an order to hurry, as to a driver pressing the accelerator
the proverb says more of it means less speed

explanation.surface: Hurry up, says the saying that claims rushing slows you down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurrying is what 'step on it' urges, and the proverb 'more haste, less speed' makes hurry a brake.

clue.text: Poles, all the same, show such mutual disgust

definitions.text: Poles, all the same, show such mutual disgust

parts.words: Poles, all the same, show such mutual disgust
parts.note: Poles looks like people from Poland, but magnetic poles of like kind push each other away

explanation.surface: Polish people, all alike, display a shared loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Like magnetic poles push each other apart, and the same word means strong distaste.

clue.text: Stella's fast friend

parts.note: Stella was the name the satirist of Gulliver's Travels gave Esther Johnson, his close friend; his surname also means fast

explanation.surface: A woman called Stella has a loyal companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan, the Dublin satirist, was the lifelong companion of Stella, and his surname means quick.

clue.text: Margery's foot

parts.note: the name Margery, stressed on its first of three syllables, is itself one metrical foot of that pattern

explanation.surface: A woman's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot is the metrical unit, not the body part: MAR-ge-ry is one long beat then two short, as in the nursery rhyme 'See-saw, Margery Daw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one stressed syllable then two unstressed ones matches how the name is spoken.

clue.text: Calmly take point before point, see?.

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
ere is an old word for before
N, north, is another compass point
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay cool: take one point after another, understand?
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is just an instruction joining the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a tranquil, untroubled way is doing things peacefully.
